provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — malicious download links and phishing URLs are observable in SMS/messaging gateway, proxy, and DNS telemetry when the actor domains are known, but mobile-side click telemetry is sparse
medium — repeated screen-capture API use by a non-graphical process is detectable via EDR behavioral analytics but generates noise
medium — keyboard hook installation and low-level input hooking are detectable via EDR API-hook and process-injection telemetry
medium — on Windows, bulk file access by extension and Telegram directory reads are detectable via file-access auditing and EDR; on mobile, local data theft is not enterprise-observable
medium — volume/removable-drive enumeration is detectable via device-arrival events and process behavior but is common in benign software

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to browser credential stores (Login Data / logins.json / Web Data) by unexpected processes is detectable via file-access and EDR telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Password Managers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to .kdbx files by non-KeePass processes is a high-signal hunt via file-access auditing and file-integrity monitoring
medium — modification of Telegram's Updater.exe (hash/signature change, unexpected write to the Telegram directory) is detectable via file-integrity monitoring and image-load signature checks

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation of Run/RunOnce values (especially the actor-specific names SunJavaHtml / DevNicJava) is directly observable via registry-modification auditing and autoruns baselining
high — DLL injection into explorer.exe (remote thread / module load of an unsigned DLL) is detectable via Sysmon EID 7/8 and EDR process-injection analytics

medium — HTTP beaconing to the named actor domains is detectable via DNS/proxy telemetry when IOCs are loaded; the ~10-second fixed-interval FurBall beacon adds a behavioral signal, but only where mobile/network egress is monitored
medium — outbound FTP/FTPS from user endpoints to external hosts is anomalous and detectable via network/firewall egress monitoring

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — actor-controlled staging sites are off-victim infrastructure; intel/brand-monitoring and lookalike-domain tracking candidate rather than endpoint detection
low — APK sideloading and install events are largely invisible to enterprise telemetry on personal devices; MDM/mobile EDR app-inventory review is a hunt candidate

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — impersonation of legitimate app identities is detectable via package-name/certificate reputation and app-store review, but requires mobile app-inventory visibility
low — Android autostart receiver registration is not exposed in standard enterprise logs; visible only via static APK analysis or mobile-threat-defense agents
low — microphone activation on mobile is invisible to enterprise logs; on Windows, unexpected process access to audio-capture APIs is a hunt candidate via EDR
low — on-demand camera capture on mobile is not enterprise-observable; static-analysis / mobile-threat-defense candidate
low — clipboard reads are near-invisible on both platforms; hunt candidate on Windows via clipboard-API monitoring
low — automated on-device collection is not exposed to enterprise telemetry; static/dynamic APK analysis candidate
low — device-fingerprinting API calls on mobile are not enterprise-observable; static-analysis candidate
low — installed-app enumeration on mobile is invisible to enterprise telemetry; static-analysis candidate
low — SMS interception/forwarding on a personal device is not enterprise-observable; account-side detection (unusual 2FA prompts, new device sign-ins) is the practical signal
low — in-app WebView credential capture is not enterprise-observable; account-side and phishing-domain intelligence are the practical signals
low — encrypted staging blends with benign archiving; hunt candidate when correlated with a preceding collection burst
low — post-install config/command fetches on mobile are not enterprise-observable; network-IOC and static-analysis candidate
low — exfil over the C2 HTTP channel on mobile is not enterprise-observable; detectable only where the C2 domains/IPs are seen in network egress logs
low — actor-controlled messaging accounts are off-victim; intel/platform-abuse-reporting candidate
